- scripts/build_static_context.sh:the embedded Python in emit_agents_index, function fragment_sections() and fragment_lines() | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: fragment_sections() does not copy the release fold's section_not_found rule (assemble_agents.py line 284, apply_block() raises FragmentError("section_not_found")), so a fragment whose target section is not a `## ` heading, and whose marker has no ` new`, is still listed under "Pending agents.d/ fragments"; test_agents_d_fragments_listed_with_sections locks this behaviour in with the a-one.md fixture.
  WHY: The index tells the model that a section will exist at release time when the fold will refuse the fragment, which is the "promising a fold that never happens" the comment says it prevents; the reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low) because `assemble_agents.py check` in CI catches such fragments in this repo, but consumer repos that skip that check get a misleading index.
- changelog.d/8254-static-context-agents-index.md:4 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The changelog says fragments that `assemble_agents.py` would refuse to fold are left out of the index, but the index parser (`scripts/build_static_context.sh:386-430, 451`) does not check whether a marker targets an existing section or uses `new`, so it lists a fragment that `assemble_agents.py:279-285` refuses to fold.
  WHY: The changelog promises that listed fragments are foldable, but the emitted index can include a fragment the assembler will skip; the reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low). The root cause is the same as the fragment_sections() finding above, but the cited file differs, so the two are kept separate.
- scripts/build_static_context.sh:333 (used by heading_lines() at 367-383) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The heading pattern requires a literal space after `##`, while the assembler accepts any whitespace there (`scripts/assemble_agents.py:99, 188-203`), so headings such as `##\tWorkflow architecture` are left out of the index.
  WHY: The index omits a section the assembler recognises, so a model relying on the index is not pointed to that section's line range; the reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low).
- scripts/build_static_context.sh:~526-528 (`if agents_truncated: emit(finish_line(...))` after the cap loop) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The truncation notice for an agents file over 8 MiB is emitted after the cap loop with no size accounting, so total output can exceed the documented 32 KiB cap (header comment and changelog.d/8254-static-context-agents-index.md line 3) by up to ~250 bytes.
  WHY: Nothing re-checks `size` after the loop; glm rated it NIT (mapped to low) and gemini raised it only as a hardening suggestion (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE 1); anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and minimax_minimax-m3 both argue that the 256-byte RESERVE already covers the cap line plus the notice, so the claim does not hold.
